articles/find-product-links.heading: A worked example: a sneaker link with two different numbers
paragraphs: The MA-1 sneaker card in this index shows product ID 7595683628. Its catalog URL ends in /495.html. Save the full link alongside the long ID. Searching the short page number in another catalog can take you to an entirely different item.

Open the listing, select the intended colour and size, then compare the side view and size label against the saved reference. If the listing shows the right shoe but no longer offers the intended size, record the size as unavailable. A similar pair found by description deserves its own entry.

articles/read-qc-photos.heading: A tape photo you can actually compare
paragraphs: Suppose a sweatshirt measures 41 cm from armpit to armpit when laid flat. Photograph both ends of the tape in the same frame. Compare that 41 cm with the flat width of a garment that fits, or roughly 82 cm with a stated garment circumference. A body chest measurement answers a different question.

articles/size-before-you-buy.heading: When the size chart is for children
paragraphs: A label such as 8Y can describe an age group while a number such as 128 can refer to height in centimetres. Read the heading on the selected listing. For shoes, check whether centimetres describe the foot or the insole before comparing a measurement.
